prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, in which neutral atoms trapped at a magic wavelength enable time and frequency measurement at the 10^-18 level of accuracy and stability

statement.case_for: I have moved from B010 to B004 as a single-part prize for Katori and Ye. In round 1 I put B010 first because a quantitative prediction preceded and organised an experimental discovery. I still believe that, but the full exchange has shifted my weighing of maturity and credit, which were precisely the two weaknesses I listed against my own candidate. B004 has an original concept (the magic-wavelength lattice, which removes the trap-induced shift while keeping many atoms in a Lamb-Dicke geometry), a realisation that delivered what the concept promised (uncertainties near 1e-18, control of many-body interactions in a degenerate Fermi gas, millimetre-scale redshift), roughly two decades of reproduction in several laboratories, and a two-name credit that maps onto idea and realisation. As someone who works with calculated and measured spectra, I find the argument that the clock's accuracy is set by controlling a specific physical shift, not by engineering alone, convincing as a physical result. That I did not rank B004 in my opening is not evidence against it; having read seven independent arguments that agree on originality, confirmation and attribution while naming the same open reservations, I think the scientific case is sound. I am not changing position because seven colleagues agree. I am changing because the answers to my own two objections to B010 are weaker than the answers available for B004's objections.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservations remain the distinctness from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes, and the credit that falls outside the pair (Takamoto and the Sr-lattice colleagues in Katori's group, and groups at PTB, NIST, SYRTE and RIKEN). I treat the first as a judgement, not a proof, and the citation should name the magic-wavelength lattice so that it states what is new. The redefinition of the second has not happened; I regard it as supporting evidence only. I also acknowledge that this is an instrument and measurement capability more than a discovery in nature, a point Danielsson presses and which I do not dismiss. Finally, choosing B004 this year does not settle B010: the correlated and superconducting states of magic-angle graphene remain, in my view, a robust discovery with a prediction behind it, and the pairing mechanism and the allocation among Bistritzer, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto and the first authors of the 2018 papers are the open points.

responses.point: Olsson ranked magic-angle graphene (B010) first and set it aside for B004 on maturity and credit rather than because the physics is less interesting.
responses.response: I came to the same place from the other side. In round 1 I defended keeping Bistritzer on the credit and I still would for B010, but your framing is fair: the same two points (age of the field and who exactly is credited) are what I listed against my own candidate. I do not think the pairing mechanism is a reason to wait indefinitely, since the discovery is the correlated states themselves, but a committee that cannot yet agree on the early experimental history, which you say you have not verified, does not have a clean allocation. I would want that settled before B010 is a first-place configuration, and I think we agree on that.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that a magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct concept whose accuracy gain of several orders of magnitude is a qualitative change, asks whether the redefinition of the second is a condition, and in round 1 doubted that DMFT shows an explained observation.
responses.response: On distinctness I accept your answer, and I would say it from my side of the field: the result is that one tunes a specific shift to zero while keeping confinement, which is a new physical regime and not only better stabilisation of a laser. On the redefinition, my answer to the chair's question is that it is supporting evidence only and not a condition; the science is not waiting on a metrology decision. On B027 your standard (a specific observation explained, not only a calculational tool) is fair and I did not meet it in my opening. I withdraw it as a configuration for this year and keep it only as a long-term candidate.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, asked me to say what result DMFT explained that other approaches could not, and states that the lattice clock is an advance in what can be measured, with no scientific reason to wait.
responses.response: I cannot give you a single decisive observation for DMFT that I would be comfortable putting in a citation. The Mott-transition picture and the treatment of correlated oxides are real, but they are results of a framework used with many methods, and the framework's strength is as a tool. That is why I no longer present it as a configuration. I agree with you that there is no scientific reason to wait on B004 and I accept your point that the pairing of Katori's idea and Ye's performance is a natural two-person credit, though I share your caution that the relative weight of the two cannot be verified from the supplied record.

responses.point: Danielsson weighs most heavily a clue found in nature, calls B004 a prize for an instrument and measurement capability, and fears choosing the more comfortable attribution over the more consequential discovery.
responses.response: I take that worry seriously because I voiced a version of it in my own candidate's favour: a tunable parameter that dials correlation strength is a new way to find things in nature. But the committee cannot choose B032 on consequence alone if, as you yourself say, the three-name allocation inside a large collaboration is something you could not verify. I made the same argument against my own B010 on allocation grounds. Where a measurement tool has opened a new regime (and tests of constants and redshift are results in nature, not only instruments), I think the instrument criterion is met. If the IceCube source associations sharpen in a year or two and the roles can be documented, I would be ready to reconsider B032.

responses.point: Kroll disclosed a doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, Ye's institution, and says the science of the clock is settled and does not depend on the redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree with the scientific half of your statement and with the answer on the redefinition. On the disclosure, I read it as a historical connection to an environment and not a personal or collaborative tie to Katori or Ye; it is properly declared, and I do not think it requires a step beyond disclosure, such as recusal, provided you remain open to the concerns about Takamoto and the other Sr groups that you raised yourself. The chair also asked about Ye under other lines: the shortlist shows Ye and Katori only under B004, so Johansson's remark about Ye appearing under other candidate lines does not match the shortlist and need not affect balance.

uncertainties: Whether the lattice-clock step is judged distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a committee judgement that I regard as favourable but unproven; the citation wording should state the magic-wavelength lattice explicitly.
Whether credit for Takamoto and other Sr or Yb groups, and for PTB, NIST, SYRTE and RIKEN, should change the names; I cannot verify the priority record from the supplied material.

What the committee would need to see before B010 is ready: a settled history of the early experiments and the first authors' roles, and some evidence on the pairing mechanism, even though I do not regard the mechanism as a condition for the discovery.
How the committee would rank alternatives if B004 were set aside; the files do not show this and I have not tried to claim that they do.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Katori, Ye or any credited name on B004 or B010 is apparent from my profile. My research on electronic structure, magnetism and correlated electrons is close to B027, B009 and B010 in subject, which is an intellectual proximity and not a documented tie; I have withdrawn B027 as a configuration. I chaired the 2025 cycle, which is not a recusal matter in my view. I am not close to atomic clock work, so I rely on colleagues' expertise for the technical details.
